**Ch 013 draft review**

- "I drew my bench near him, and made some friendly signs and hints." — The source continues: "At first he little noticed these advances; but presently, upon my referring to his last night's hospitalities, he made out to ask me whether we were again to be bedfellows. - "I would remonstrate; but he silenced me by pouring them into my pockets." — "I would remonstrate" vs. source's "I was going to remonstrate." Slightly odd tense but not structurally broken.

- "offered him burnt biscuit with Queequeg" — This is a compression artifact (the idol is the referent of "him," and "with Queequeg" is garbled from the source's "offered him burnt biscuit with Queequeg" — actually this is verbatim from the source, so no issue introduced by the draft).

- "Thus, then, in our hearts' honeymoon, lay I and Queequeg — a cosy, loving pair." — The source has "But we did not go to sleep without some little chat. How it is I know not..." then the bed-confidences paragraph, then the closing line. The draft cuts "But we did not go to sleep without some little chat" and the bridge sentence. The remaining "How it is I know not; but there is no place like a bed for confidential disclosures between friends. Thus, then..." still parses — the "Thus, then" still follows from the general observation. No confusion.

For now I liked nothing better than to have Queequeg smoking by me..." The draft cuts the pivot entirely and gives only the bare fact of assent. A reader has no reason to find this notable — but does the sentence itself parse and make sense? Yes, it does. It's less ornamented, not broken. No finding.

- "I begged him to go on." — Source: "I begged him to go on and tell it. He gladly complied. Though at the time I but ill comprehended not a few of his words, yet subsequent disclosures, when I had become more familiar with his broken phraseology, now enable me to present the whole story such as it may prove in the mere skeleton I give." The draft ends the chapter here, cutting the narratorial gloss about how Ishmael is reconstructing Queequeg's story from later knowledge.
